reviews.one_line_contribution: A read-time gate that skips memory injection whenever the top-k retrieved experience items recommend different next actions (a cheap action-template consistency score, no extra LLM call), plus the accompanying claim — tested head-to-head against six reimplemented item-level controls on organically accumulated ALFWorld banks — that harm from agent experience memory is predicted by disagreement within the retrieved set rather than by any per-item property.
reviews.closest_prior_work: RSCB-MC, arXiv:2604.27283, 'Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents' (VERIFIED via s2cli, S2, 2026-04-30, 2 citations). Its abstract says the controller 'decides whether an agent should use no memory, inject the top resolution, summarize multiple candidates, perform high-precision or high-recall retrieval, abstain, or ask for feedback' — a learned read-time decision over the retrieved candidate set, including abstention and an explicit multi-candidate action, not a per-item utility score. The proposal's framing that 'every proposed defence acts on items' is therefore already false for its own baseline (f), and the surviving contribution shrinks to 'a hand-designed set-consistency statistic beats a learned bandit controller at zero extra calls' — far weaker than the title. Three further verified threats: StateFuse (arXiv:2607.05844, VERIFIED, whose own summary says it is 'best supported as a safer public memory contract for contradiction surfacing, abstention, and auditable correction') already couples surfaced retrieval-set disagreement to abstention; 'When Personal Memory Has No Single Answer' (arXiv:2608.13921, VERIFIED) already 'frames conflict handling as recognizing underdetermination, retaining conflicting evidence, and acting without forcing a definitive answer' — the abstain-under-set-disagreement policy, in personal-memory QA; and 'When Correct Demonstrations Hurt' (arXiv:2605.26350, VERIFIED via HF, 2026-05-25), uncited here, already argues ICL harm is a property of the effective evidence mixture rather than of individual exemplar correctness — the set-not-item thesis, one domain over. None runs this exact experiment, so the work is incremental rather than scooped, but it cannot be sold as the first to name the unit.
reviews.strongest_objection: The gate's measured benefit is not separable from injecting less. This program's own starting position is that injection volume, not memory content, was the causal lever: cutting from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank. The gate reduces injected tokens to zero exactly on the retrievals where it fires. With no rate-matched random-abstention arm and no token-matched placebo, P2's '70 percent of paired broken count removed' is precisely what a coin-flip gate firing at the same rate would produce in a regime where memory is one-sidedly harmful (pilot: fixed 0, broke 6-7). Two flaws compound it. (i) P3 is near-tautological: the gate is the identity map on agree-right sets, so 'zero clean-setting cost' is true by construction — the only empirical content is the edit-distance proxy's false-positive rate, which is not what the title advertises. (ii) The set-versus-item dichotomy is close to definitionally rigged: a 'disagree' set is essentially one containing a wrong item alongside a right one, so the set label is a near-deterministic function of the item labels. P1 can only be won by restricting the item-level model to marginals; an item-level model with set-aggregated features ('any wrong item present', 'count of wrong items') would likely fit as well. The defensible finding is much smaller: disagreement is an observable read-time proxy for the unobservable presence of a wrong item. Separately, the primary configuration is k=3 — the exact setting this program already measured as harm-free — so the pre-registered 'fallback to k=5 if harm is below the MDE' guarantees the reported condition was selected because it manufactured harm, which reads as garden-pathing rather than pre-registration.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the primary contrast gate versus rate-matched random abstention, not gate versus ungated injection, and add a token-matched placebo (inject k neutral items on disagree sets); without these the headline number is uninterpretable given this program's own volume result. (2) Add a top-1-only / reduced-k arm so 'abstain' is tested against 'inject less', not only against 'inject all'. (3) Respecify P1 so the item-level competitor includes set-aggregated item features (any-wrong, count-wrong, min per-item utility); if the set label still wins the LRT the claim is real, otherwise report the honest version. (4) Drop 'zero clean-setting cost' from the headline and pre-register instead the consistency score's false-positive rate on agree-right sets. (5) Fix k in the pilot's harmful regime up front and report the disagree-cell base rate from a small pilot before committing the confirmatory arms. (6) Cut scope by roughly an order of magnitude: one bank checkpoint and one backbone for the ten-arm head-to-head, other checkpoints/backbones only for arms (a), (b), (i); drop WebShop or demote it to a limitation. (7) Replace or drop arXiv:2608.07429 (TEPA) and arXiv:2608.10509 (provenance gating), which return 'not found' on both channels, and cite 2608.13921 and 2605.26350 as the closest statements of the set-level idea.
reviews.missing_baseline: Rate-matched random abstention: abstain on a randomly chosen subset of retrievals at the gate's empirical firing rate, same tasks, seeds and banks. This is the control that separates 'disagreement predicts harm' from 'injecting less on some fraction of retrievals removes harm', and it is the first thing an area chair will demand given that this program has already established volume as the causal lever. Closely related and also absent: a token-matched placebo injection on disagree sets, and a top-1-only (reduce k instead of abstain) arm. The plan's 'no memory' and 'inject-always' references and the oracle ceiling do not substitute — none holds the abstention rate fixed while randomizing which retrievals are skipped.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's check is unusually thorough for this genre — it names channels, queries and IDs and flags 2606.01435 as unverified — and deserves credit; but two of its load-bearing citations do not exist on either channel. It asserts 's2cli verification: 2608.07429 confirmed as TEPA'; my `s2cli.py paper 2608.07429` returned 'not found on S2 or HF', and a targeted TEPA search returned nothing matching (2608.06811, 2607.18970, 2607.14890, 2607.13157, 2606.18728, 2606.10677, 2605.26252, 2605.06527). Baseline (d) rests on an id I could not verify, and the check's claim to have verified it does not reproduce. Likewise arXiv:2608.10509 ('provenance gating', another of the six control families) returned 'not found on S2 or HF', and a targeted search surfaced nothing matching (2608.15008, 2606.24775, 2606.18829, 2605.06132, 2602.16313, 2603.02240). My searches, all via the s2cli channel (WebSearch/WebFetch unavailable this session): (a) 'retrieved set disagreement gate abstain agent memory conflicting retrieved items' — 2608.04574, 2607.10608, 2607.05844, 2606.26511, 2605.30087, 2605.05583, 2605.06527, plus older 2406.13805, 2306.07934; no retrieved-set consistency gate for experience memory. (b) --recent: 'consistency among retrieved examples predicts harm selective retrieval augmentation abstain when retrieved evidence conflicts' — 2605.30087, 2605.29084, 2605.01302, 2604.05467, 2604.18847; RAG-side only. (c) named method: 'MemRL learned per-item utility filtering experience memory reinforcement learning agent' — verified 2601.03192 as MemRL with a 'two-phase retrieval mechanism with learned utility values' (83 citations), confirming the proposal's characterization; also 2607.20553, 2605.13486, 2601.20831. (d) --recent: 'agreement between retrieved demonstrations self-consistency signal decide whether to use in-context examples' — 2605.26350, 2605.07654, 2605.05166, 2601.07058. (e) 'provenance gating path trust reranking agent memory ... steerable reliance dial' — as above. IDs VERIFIED by lookup: 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, E-P-R), 2605.09330 (The Trap of Trajectory / CAMEL — the proposal's own check lists this id twice under two titles without noting they are one paper), 2604.27283 (RSCB-MC), 2601.03192 (MemRL), 2607.05844 (StateFuse), 2601.05107 ('Controllable Memory Usage', ACL — reliance as a user-controllable dial, as described), 2606.22844 (RaMem, 'Contextual Reinstatement for Long-term Agentic Memory'), 2603.09641 (PRECEPT, Bayesian source reliability and threshold-based rule invalidation), 2605.29463 (Honest Lying), 2605.20926 (MemConflict — note it 'injects semantically similar distractors to create competition among memory candidates', i.e. it already manipulates set-level competition, though as a conversational-memory diagnostic), 2608.13921 (When Personal Memory Has No Single Answer), 2605.06527 (STALE), 2608.04574, 2605.05583. NOT FOUND on either channel: 2608.07429, 2608.10509, 2606.01435 (self-admitted). Two near misses the check missed and should cite: arXiv:2605.30087 (Selective QA over Conflicting Multi-Source Personal Memory) and arXiv:2605.26350. Net: the core mechanism search is genuinely empty for agent experience memory in task execution, so novelty is not dead, but the idea is a transfer of a well-worn RAG/self-consistency mechanism into a new domain, and the differentiation argument leans on two baseline citations that appear not to exist.
